title.en: Prompt Caching: Why a Cache Hit Costs 90% Less

description.en: As context windows push past a million tokens in 2026, re-sending the same system prompt or document on every call gets expensive fast. Prompt caching fixes that — learn the one multiplier that makes a repeated prefix nearly free.

story_variants.en:
## Paying For The Same Tokens Twice

"Say your app sends a 20,000-token system prompt with *every single call*," Vaathiyaar says. "A customer-support bot, a codebase-aware assistant, a long house style guide — the prefix never changes, but a naive API call bills you full price for it, again and again, call after call."

### The Fix: Let The Server Remember The Prefix

**Prompt caching** stores the model's internal representation of a prefix the first time you send it. Every later call that starts with that *exact same* prefix gets a **cache hit**: the server skips re-processing those tokens and charges a fraction of the normal input price for them.

On Claude's API in 2026, a cache hit costs **0.1x** the standard input-token rate — a **90% discount** on every token the cache serves. Only the *new* part of the prompt (today's actual question) is billed at full price.

```
normal call:    20,000 prefix tokens @ 1.0x + 50 new tokens @ 1.0x
cached call:     20,000 prefix tokens @ 0.1x + 50 new tokens @ 1.0x
```

### Savings Compound With Prefix Size

The bigger the shared prefix relative to the new content, the more a cache hit saves — which is exactly why prompt caching matters *more*, not less, as context windows grow toward a million tokens. A tiny 200-token prompt barely benefits; a 20,000-token document pasted into every call benefits enormously.

> **Vaathiyaar's rule:** if the same tokens are going out the door on every call, they shouldn't be billed at full price every time. Prompt caching is that principle turned into an API flag.

Today you compute exactly how much a cache hit saves, in dollars and in percent.
